request: Enrich the whole arena city, including unseen districts, with narrow populated commercial streets, coherent irregular quarters and natural-looking physical world boundaries.

The first belt of buildings is too distant to enclose pedestrian streets around the main landmark.
A thin, regularly spaced line of exterior characters does not read as groups buying, waiting, talking or carrying goods.
Canopies, storage, carts and people do not overlap in depth as they do in the reference foreground.
preservedComposition: The arena footprint, facade, seating bowl, imperial box and service circulation.
The elevated comparison camera and the left canal / bridge, rear temple and right aqueduct landmark order.
A clear ceremonial entry axis and continuous access to the exterior arcades.
revisionCriteria: Close retail frontages and clustered multi-row event markets with actual narrow passages.
Goods and workspaces arranged around retail activities rather than uniformly scattered objects.
Denser crowds concentrated around stalls, queues and social groups, with moving merchants and porters.
Corresponding elevated views and full-size eye-height views, followed by actual first-person traversal.
status: Completed source and final WebGPU visual review; accepted with the documented visual and performance limits.

observations: An enclosed commercial lane presents complete counters, supported awnings, talking groups and a walker, with temple and aqueduct in depth.

This is a wider civic space rather than a narrow market alley.

The retaining wall hides most water from this eye-height position; the paved apron remains broad.
Trading counters, modeled bread and produce, crates and baskets frame a court with a basket porter and small social groups.
Open paving between these activity nodes remains broader and cleaner than the primary illustration.
Close complete houses, wall returns and a bend form a narrower inhabited passage with a porter, walkers and groups in the next court.
Recessed windows, wall thickness and cast shadows remain readable at human scale.

A dark irregular paving join is conspicuous along the curved street overlay; no visible unsupported geometry or blocking gap was identified in this image.

This camera demonstrates the market and gate approach, not a direct river view.
Supported columns, stone beams, visible roof rafters, a fountain basin, planted beds, seated residents and walkers make a distinct public garden room beneath the aqueduct.

Deep repeated piers and arches establish the curved interior gallery, with one walker and a mounted torch visible.
